message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell** (sometimes referred to as a **syncytium**).  
In many tissues you’ll find specific examples, such as:

| Tissue | Typical multinucleated cell | Function |
|--------|-----------------------------|----------|
| Muscle | Skeletal muscle fibers | Contraction |
| Immune | Giant cells (e.g., Langhans giant cells) | Phagocytosis / inflammation |
| Placenta | Syncytiotrophoblast | Nutrient exchange between mother and fetus |

So if you’re looking for a general term, “multinucleated” or “syncytium” is the right one.
